notes.fact: Iran's Revolutionary Guards navy says two tankers hit mines and caught fire in the southern Hormuz route; it named no vessels and gave no casualty details.
Iranian naval statements carried by IRIB say three tankers hit mines in separate incidents; the IRGC says six tankers have burned and are sinking since Sunday.
notes.key: claim:iranian army navy and irgc navy
notes.claim_by: party:Iranian army navy and IRGC Navy

notes.fact: Iran's Nour News, citing IRNA, says the IRGC Navy declared the southern route mined, calls it a response to the US blockade and warns shipowners off.
The UK maritime monitor UKMTO reports a tanker leaving the strait was hit by an unknown projectile, causing an engine-room fire; all crew are accounted for and none were hurt.
CBS notes it is unclear whether the UKMTO-reported projectile strike and Iran's mine-strike claim describe the same tanker.
UKMTO set the regional maritime threat level to severe, citing IRGC attacks, attempted attacks and harassment of shipping near Hormuz.
Reuters says it could not independently verify the Revolutionary Guards' claim that two tankers exploded after striking naval mines.
Bahrain's military says it intercepted several Iranian attacks; AFP says sirens sounded and it was the second strike on Bahrain in three days.
notes.event: Iranian drones at US base in Bahrain

notes.fact: US Central Command says it shot down two Iranian drones aimed at Bahrain on Friday, with no injuries or damage, rejecting Iran's claim of destroying a US radar.
notes.event: Iranian drones at US base in Bahrain

notes.fact: Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Jordan and Egypt condemned Iran's Sunday attacks on Bahrain, expressing solidarity with it.
notes.event: Iranian drones at US base in Bahrain

notes.fact: Reuters reports there was no immediate US or Bahraini confirmation of the IRGC's claim, and says diplomacy has yet to produce a breakthrough.
notes.event: Iranian drones at US base in Bahrain

notes.fact: Iran's foreign ministry spokesman says Tehran will keep responding to US military action and is not waiting on anyone, while diplomacy stays stalled.
notes.event: Iranian drones at US base in Bahrain

notes.fact: BBC says US officials told CBS the US struck Iran's Qeshm Island earlier this week, and that the June preliminary deal collapsed, with the US blockade reinstated.
Saudi-backed Yemeni forces say they are leaving Dhubab airport and the Bab al-Mandab area, which leaves the strait under Houthi control.
The National says the pullback is meant to secure Aden and break the Houthi siege of Taiz, and that Houthi strikes have hit Saudi ports, airports and Aramco sites.
Houthi-run media says the group has taken control of the area; All India Radio notes Saudi Arabia had not yet commented on the withdrawal.
The Houthis say they pose no threat to international shipping in the waterway but will keep targeting Saudi vessels.
SOFX says the Houthis target only Saudi and Israeli-linked ships for now, and container lines have returned to the Red Sea.
Al-Arabi al-Jadid reports, via Informed Comment, that Houthi forces said they were within a few miles of Aden and had fired ballistic missiles at the city.
Russia's defence ministry says it downed 1,336 Ukrainian drones overnight; AFP's tally of Russian statements makes that the second-highest daily figure this year.
notes.event: Crimea bridge strike and drone barrage

notes.fact: Moscow's mayor says about 600 drones were intercepted on approach to Moscow; the barrage followed Ukrainian strikes on a petrochemical plant and a refinery.
notes.event: Crimea bridge strike and drone barrage
notes.claim_by: party:Moscow mayor and Russian defence ministry

notes.fact: Al Arabiya reports the Moscow-appointed Crimean official confirmed the hit and gave no word on casualties; Kyiv has targeted the bridge several times since 2022.
notes.event: Crimea bridge strike and drone barrage

notes.fact: AFP says last week's Abu Dhabi talks produced no result; Putin repeated hardline territorial demands, and Zelensky says the US proposed Ukraine cede land for NATO membership.
China's foreign ministry confirmed Xi will hold a three-way meeting with Trump and Putin in Shenzhen on November 19, giving no agenda; the Kremlin and White House had already confirmed.
Korea Times reports Trump wants to discuss cutting nuclear arsenals and is expected to raise the Iran war, while US officials say Ukraine is not expected to feature.
Kremlin spokesman Peskov told TASS the three-way meeting is agreed for November 19 on the margins of the APEC summit in Shenzhen.
Romania's prime minister says drones struck three merchant ships near the Sulina canal; Romanian jets were scrambled twice, and Russia denies targeting Ukraine's neighbours.
notes.event: Drone strikes on ships off Romania

notes.fact: A fourth ship, the Palau-flagged Larissa 1, was hit by a drone on November 13 about 12 km off the coast; Romania has not named who launched the drones.
notes.event: Drone strikes on ships off Romania

notes.fact: Pakistan's Dawn carries the Reuters report that drones hit three ships near Sulina, adding that Romanian officials did not identify the drones' origin but tied them to Russia's war.
notes.event: Drone strikes on ships off Romania

notes.fact: The Liberian-flagged container ship Contship Jet sank after naval drones hit it off Bulgaria on October 28, according to the Bulgarian government.
Australia, Canada, Italy and the UK urge Israel to allow rapid, unimpeded aid, saying 150,000 tents are held at the border; Hamas-led authorities say rain swept away tents.
Al Jazeera adds that a UN humanitarian team called flood deaths preventable, and that an Israeli strike on Nasser Hospital on Thursday killed six people.
Spain's Democrata says the UN reports most of the tents are blocked at Al Arish in Egypt by authorisation procedures and limited crossing capacity.
The EU voiced grave concern on Saturday and urged Israel to reopen all Gaza border crossings.
AFRICOM says it carried out an airstrike on al-Shabaab on November 12 near Leego, about 114 km northwest of Mogadishu, in coordination with Somalia's government.
AFRICOM lists an earlier strike on al-Shabaab on November 5, after strikes on October 21 and 23 near Bulo Bashiir.
CISA, FBI, HHS, USDA and DOT warn that attackers are targeting internet-exposed refrigeration controllers in grocery and cold storage, forcing heating and defrost cycles; the activity is global.
France's blood service EFS confirmed an incident at a refrigeration provider changed temperature and defrost settings at three blood-storage sites.
A forum summary says France's CERT-FR alert warned that end-of-life, internet-exposed controllers were very likely to be compromised again; US agencies name no vendor.
SC World says the federal advisory draws on suspected attacks on European supermarkets, French blood banks and up to six US military commissaries; the Pentagon is investigating.

The FBI alerts page lists an FBI-EPA notice on attacks on internet-facing Rockwell/Allen-Bradley MicroLogix 1100 and 1400 controllers at water utilities, and a joint advisory on Iranian-affiliated actors exploiting such controllers.

notes.fact: CISA, FBI, NSA and partners warn that China-based Integrity Technology Group enables actors targeting critical infrastructure worldwide, including healthcare, manufacturing and government, using botnets and VPN infrastructure.
notes.hotspot: cyber: new China-linked Integrity Tech advisory

notes.fact: Ridgecrest Regional Hospital in California confirmed a cyber incident and took systems offline; phones and pharmacy payments have returned, but a prescription backlog and full recovery remain unclear.
Monadnock Community Hospital in Peterborough, New Hampshire diverted ambulances amid a suspected cyber incident; the emergency department stayed open and emergency surgeries continued.
notes.hotspot: cyber: new Monadnock Community Hospital outage
notes.event: New Hampshire hospital suspected cyber incident

notes.fact: Microsoft says the global outage from November 12 stemmed from network capacity changes, not a cyberattack; hospitals in the US and NHS bodies lost email and paging.
notes.hotspot: cyber: new Microsoft 365 outage (not attributed to attack)

notes.fact: A low-profile site reports the Homeland Security Secretary called the Nov 13 aviation disruption a telecom outage, and says officials have not tied it to a cyberattack.
notes.hotspot: cyber: new US air traffic outage Nov 13 (not attributed to attack)

notes.fact: Konbriefing lists a ransomware attack on Medi Porta in Chur, Switzerland that exposed sensitive data from local storage, with medical care continuing.
notes.hotspot: cyber: new Medi Porta ransomware, Switzerland
